questions.question: 波拉尼奥《2666》从头到尾没有查出边境连环杀女案的凶手。按一种对这部小说的解读，这样处理的用意是什么？
options: 作者在书完成前去世，凶手的身份来不及写出
给出凶手就暗示「抓住他就结束了」，而这里的恶是许多零件叠成的
作者想留下一个悬念，好让读者自己推理出真凶就是狱中的克劳斯·哈斯
作者认为真实案件已经破了，没有必要在小说里重复
questions.explanation: 按「阿尔钦博托原则」，学者的虚荣、警察的懒、工厂压成本、政客要选票，每样都不足以杀人，退开看却是一张脸；给出凶手，这张脸就变回一堆零件。「未完成」确实是一项争议，但不给凶手是贯穿五部的结构设计，而现实中的华雷斯城案件也长期未破。
questions.question_en: Roberto Bolaño's 2666 never identifies the killer behind the border femicides. On one reading of the novel, what is the point of leaving it unsolved?
options_en: Bolaño died before finishing the book, so the killer's identity was never written
Naming a killer would imply that catching him ends it, when the evil here is an arrangement built from many small parts
Bolaño wanted readers to deduce for themselves that Klaus Haas is the real killer
Bolaño considered the real cases already solved, so there was no need to repeat it in fiction
questions.explanation_en: Under the 'Arcimboldo principle', vanity, police laziness, factory cost-cutting and politicians' vote-seeking are each harmless up close but form a face from a distance; naming a killer would break the face back into parts. Whether the book is unfinished is a real debate, but withholding the killer is a structural design across all five parts, and the real Juárez killings largely went unsolved.

questions.question: 《2666》第四部用三百多页、几乎同一句式罗列一百多名被杀女工。对这种写法，哪种理解最贴合它的设计？
options: 它用重复让每个受害者都打动读者，使同情随人数不断放大
把读者的疲劳变成论据：开始跳读死者，正是那座城市对她们做的事
它是作者在堆积未及删减的调查材料，属于未完成稿的痕迹
它模仿警方档案的格式，目的是让读者像侦探一样从细节里一步步推出凶手
questions.explanation: 目录体让读者亲身经历从逐字读到扫读的麻木，同时每段留一个不肯被格式吃掉的细节在麻木时扎一下。这种麻木也呼应心理麻木的研究：受害者变多，同情并不随之放大，甚至变弱。
questions.question_en: Part four of 2666 lists over a hundred murdered women across some three hundred pages in nearly identical sentences. Which reading best fits what this form is designed to do?
options_en: It uses repetition so each victim moves the reader, making sympathy grow with every case
It turns the reader's fatigue into an argument: once you start skimming the dead, you are doing what the city did to them
It is unedited research material piled up, a trace of an unfinished draft
It mimics police files so readers can deduce the killer from the details like detectives
questions.explanation_en: The catalogue form makes readers live through the slide from careful reading to skimming, while each entry keeps one detail that refuses the format and pricks you mid-numbness. This matches research on psychic numbing: as victims multiply, compassion does not scale up and may even shrink.

questions.question: 《2666》开头，两位文学教授在伦敦街头把出租车司机踢到不动，嘴里一边供应理由：为朋友、为被压迫的妇女、为文明。这一场在全书主题上演示了什么？
options: 这是一场正当防卫，作者借此为学者们的行为辩护
暴力从不缺理由，人文教养也可能只产出更精致的辩解
它说明伦敦的种族冲突是全书暴力的真正根源
受过高等教育的人一旦被冒犯，往往会比普通人更冲动、更失控
questions.explanation: 自由间接引语贴着施暴者的脑子走，让读者一边看到皮鞋落下、一边听见人道主义词汇源源不断。先用一百多页让读者喜欢他们，再让他们施暴，逼出全书的追问：读最好的书，到底让人变好了没有。
questions.question_en: Early in 2666, two literature professors kick a London cab driver until he stops moving, all the while supplying reasons — for their friend, for oppressed women, for civilization. What does this scene demonstrate about the book's themes?
options_en: It is self-defense, and Bolaño uses it to vindicate the scholars
Violence never lacks reasons — restraint does; humanistic culture may only produce more refined self-justification
It shows that racial conflict in London is the true root of the book's violence
Highly educated people are more impulsive than others once they feel insulted
questions.explanation_en: Free indirect speech tracks the attackers' minds, so we see the shoes land while hearing a steady stream of humanitarian language. Having made us like them for a hundred pages, Bolaño forces the book's question: does reading the best books make anyone better?
